title: Improving the accuracy of medical diagnosis with causal machine learning

content.abstract_summary: Demonstrates that associative machine learning algorithms make systematic, safety-critical errors in clinical diagnostics due to confounding and selection bias, whereas counterfactual and causal machine learning formulations consistently outperform associative models and approach expert human physician accuracy.
key_findings: Purely associative ML models confuse correlation with causation, failing when presented with rare disease presentations or confounded clinical markers
Counterfactual reasoning via Pearl's do-calculus enables algorithms to query 'what if' scenarios accurately
Causal ML achieves top-quarter physician-level diagnostic accuracy (F1 score significantly higher than standard associative deep learning)
Proves mathematically why counterfactual validity is essential for clinical decision-support and synthetic patient simulation
limitations: Requires explicit causal graph specification or strong assumptions for causal discovery

extracted_claims.text: Associative algorithms suffer from systematic errors when observational correlations do not reflect causal relationships. Causal reasoning rectifies these limitations.

gaps_addressed: Provides mathematical and empirical rationale for requiring counterfactual / causal validity in synthetic patients and digital twins in Pillar 4 (M4.2)

provenance.notes: Added 2026-08-29 by Antigravity review. Foundational benchmark paper demonstrating why causal ML is required for clinical decision support and synthetic digital twins.
